content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Understand and use open, close, look, listen, read, and write. Model: “Please open your book and look at page six.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use classroom instructions clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Please open your book and look at page six.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where classroom instructions is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

language_focus: Understand and use open, close, look, listen, read, and write.
objectives: Understand and use open, close, look, listen, read, and write.
Use teacher instructions in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about classroom instructions.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about classroom instructions. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What should the learner do after listening?
listening.transcript: Open your notebook, listen, and write one word.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Stress the action words: OPEN, LIS-ten, WRITE. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Stress the action words: OPEN, LIS-ten, WRITE.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about classroom instructions.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using classroom instructions; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise classroom instructions?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Please open your book and look at page six.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about classroom instructions with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about classroom instructions. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Please open your book and look at page six. Submit your draft first.
